Historically, they have offered a lower-risk way to preserve capital while maintaining liquidity and earning interest exempt from state and local taxes. The NEOS Enhanced Income 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF (CSHI) —a top percentile performer in the Morningstar US Fund Ultrashort Bond Category (based on total return for the three years ending 9/30/2026 among 227 funds in that category)—aims to build on that foundation. CSHI seeks: Higher income from cash-like allocations Lower correlation to interest rates A higher degree of tax efficiency How CSHI Seeks Additional Income While Aiming to Maintain a Low Risk Profile CSHI pairs the stability and liquidity of 1–3 month U.S. Treasury bills with a data-driven options strategy designed to enhance income while aiming to maintain a low risk profile. The strategy rests on three pillars: Disciplined options approach: Deep out-of-the-money put spreads are established and rolled weekly to seek consistent premium income. Data-driven risk management: Historical market-return patterns help guide strike selection and support a low probability of option losses. Additional tax efficiency: SPX Index options offer deep liquidity and may provide greater tax efficiency than interest income. How CSHI's Option Strategy Works CSHI leverages a data-driven put spread option overlay to seek enhanced tax efficient monthly income. Short OTM SPX put spread construction The graph illustrates the risk-and-reward profile of an out-of-the-money SPX put spread. Premium received provides income, while the purchased put limits potential losses if the SPX declines significantly. Source: NEOS Investments. Each spread is constructed in two steps to seek income while defining downside risk: Step 1: Short put is sold to generate premium. Step 2: Long put is purchased to limit the loss potential of the sold put. Step 1 + Step 2 = one spread position Using multiple spread positions may help generate tax-efficient income while diversifying exposure across strike levels to support the strategy's low-risk profile. Positioning in the Left Tail The distribution of rolling one-week S&P 500 Index returns shows that most weekly market moves have clustered near the center of the range. By positioning its four short put-spread levels farther into the less frequently occurring left tail, the strategy seeks to generate income beyond the portfolio's underlying T-Bill yield while maintaining defined downside exposure over each one-week holding period. Story Continues SPX rolling 1-week returns distribution with CSHI put spread levels Distribution of SPX rolling 1-week returns, with CSHI's four put spread levels positioned in the left tail. Source: NEOS Investments. Historically, these downside levels have been reached very infrequently: Since 2000, the SPX has reached the first short put-spread level in just 1.49% of rolling one-week periods. That frequency falls to 0.18% across two consecutive weeks. Across three consecutive weeks, it drops to just 0.02%, illustrating how rarely declines of this magnitude have persisted. Navigating Sharp Market Selloffs CSHI's track record puts its low-risk profile in perspective. During the early-2025 "Liberation Day" selloff, CSHI fell just 1.5% before recovering, while the S&P 500 Index dropped roughly 16%—demonstrating that CSHI's option overlay was able to maintain a relatively low risk profile through a sharp market decline. CSHI vs. 1-3 month T-bills vs. S&P 500 total return, March–May 2025 Measured against the S&P 500, CSHI's drawdown during the Liberation Day 2025 selloff was minimal. Source: NEOS Investments. CSHI vs. 1-3 month T-bills total return, March–May 2025 Viewed on its own narrow y-axis, CSHI's roughly 1.5% move looks dramatic; it recovered and finished the period ahead of T-bills (1.25% vs. 1.07%). Source: NEOS Investments. Over the longer term, from inception on August 29, 2022, through September 30, 2026, CSHI outperformed the Bloomberg U.S. 1–3 Month Treasury Bill Index, with a cumulative total return of 23.92% versus 19.97% for the index. CSHI vs. 1-3 month T-bills total return since inception Total return from inception, August 29, 2022, through September 30, 2026: CSHI 23.92% vs. Bloomberg US Treasury Bills 1-3 Month Index 19.97%. Source: NEOS Investments. Put Short-Term Cash to Work with Enhanced Income Potential For investors looking to do more with their cash allocation, NEOS Enhanced Income 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF (CSHI) combines a portfolio of 1–3 month U.S. Treasury bills with a data-driven options strategy designed to enhance monthly income, improve tax efficiency, and reduce sensitivity to interest-rate movements—all within a liquid, accessible ETF. CSHI offers: Enhanced monthly income potential The potential for greater tax efficiency Potentially lower correlation to interest rates About NEOS Investments Headquartered in Westport, CT, NEOS was founded by a team of options-based ETF pioneers who previously created and managed some of the largest options-based ETFs currently in the market. With 30+ professionals firmwide and decades of combined investment experience, NEOS is a global asset manager that utilizes quantitative approaches that seek to deliver investment solutions known for high monthly income potential and tax efficiency across core portfolio exposures and asset classes. NEOS is an award-winning ETF issuer: QQQI was named "Best New Active ETF" at the 2025 ETF.com Awards, IAUI was named "Best New Options Income ETF" at the 2026 ETF.com Awards, and NEOS Investments was named "Best Options Strategies ETF Issuer ($1bn-$10bn)" at the 2025 ETF Express U.S. Awards and "Best Options Strategies ETF Issuer ($10bn+)" at the 2026 ETF Express U.S. Awards.
